prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a people judged in Zephaniah 2: Philistines, Moab, Ammon, Assyria, or the Nile land of Cush
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a people judged in Zephaniah 2 (Philistines, Moab, Ammon, the Ethiopians of Cush on the Nile, Assyria)
prompts.note: Bible Ethiopia (Cush) lay mostly in today's Sudan, reaching into southern Egypt; modern Ethiopia is not counted.
prompts.summary: Zephaniah 2 calls Judah to seek meekness, then names the peoples who will be judged: the Philistine cities of Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod and Ekron, Moab and Ammon, the Ethiopians, and Assyria with its capital Nineveh. The Bible's Ethiopia, or Cush, was the Nile land south of Egypt, mostly today's Sudan, not modern Ethiopia.

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: The Lord will destroy Assyria and make Nineveh a desolation (Zephaniah 2:13).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Ashkelon, Ashdod and Ekron were Philistine cities (Zephaniah 2:4).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Moab and the children of Ammon shall be as Sodom (Zephaniah 2:8-9).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Gaza shall be forsaken (Zephaniah 2:4); it lies in the Gaza Strip.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Ye Ethiopians also (Zeph 2:12): the Bible Dictionary's Cush began at Syene, today Aswan in Egypt.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: Ye Ethiopians also, ye shall be slain (Zephaniah 2:12); Bible Ethiopia, or Cush, ran south from Syene along the Nile, mostly today's Sudan.

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country whose Global Histories chronology names a senior married couple as its first missionaries.
prompts.text_original: In several African countries the first missionaries were not young elders but senior married couples. Pin an African country whose Global Histories chronology names a senior married couple as its first missionaries.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Ghana, Nigeria, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Liberia, Benin, Cameroon, Togo
prompts.summary: Senior couples opened the Church in much of Africa: the Cannons and Mabeys in Ghana and Nigeria in 1978, the Hutchings in Zaire in 1986, the Palmers in Liberia in 1987, the Paynes in Cameroon in 1991 and the Findlays in Benin and Togo in 1999.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: In late 1978 the Cannons and the Mabeys, two senior couples, arrived as the first missionaries in Ghana and Nigeria.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: Edwin and Janath Cannon and Rendell and Rachel Mabey began missionary work in Nigeria in November 1978.

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: The first missionaries to Zaire, Ralph and Jean Hutchings, a senior couple, arrived in Kinshasa in February 1986.

answers.name: Liberia
answers.fact: A senior couple, J. Duffy and Jocelyn Palmer, opened missionary work in Liberia on July 3, 1987.

answers.name: Benin
answers.fact: DeMoine A. and Joyce Findlay became the first missionary couple called to Benin and Togo in February 1999; the Davises were the first couple to live in Benin, in 2001.

answers.name: Cameroon
answers.fact: The first senior missionary couple, Paul Dee and Arlene Payne, were called from Nigeria to Cameroon on September 5, 1991.

answers.name: Togo
answers.fact: Senior missionaries DeMoine A. and Joyce Findlay arrived in Lome from the Cote d'Ivoire Abidjan Mission in February 1999.

prompts.display_text: Pin a European or African country where a temple was dedicated before the year 2000.
prompts.text_original: A European or African country where a temple was dedicated in the 20th century (before the year 2000).
prompts.summary: Before 2000 only six European or African countries had a dedicated temple: Switzerland (1955), the United Kingdom (1958), Germany and Sweden (1985), South Africa (1985) and Spain (1999). Every other temple on those continents came in the 21st century.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Bern Switzerland Temple, 1955, first in Europe.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: London England (1958) and Preston England (1998).

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Freiberg (1985) and Frankfurt (1987).

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Stockholm Sweden Temple, 1985.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Johannesburg South Africa Temple, 1985, first in Africa.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Madrid Spain Temple, March 1999.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory outside Europe and the US where a current apostle lived while leading a mission or an Area (Oct 2026).
prompts.text_original: A country or territory outside Europe and the United States where a member of the First Presidency or Quorum of the Twelve, as of October 2026, lived while presiding over a mission or serving in an Area presidency.
prompts.citation: Official leader biographies and Church News, read 4 Nov 2026 (Holland died 27 Dec 2025; Causse led only the Europe Area, Gilbert led no mission or Area abroad)
prompts.summary: Before their calls to the Twelve, many current apostles lived abroad on Church assignment: Oaks in the Philippines, Christofferson in Mexico, Stevenson in Japan, Renlund in South Africa, Gong in Hong Kong, and Andersen and Soares in Brazil. Oaks went as a sitting apostle in 2002 to live among the Saints for two years. Chile is no longer an answer: Jeffrey R. Holland, who presided there, died December 27, 2025.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Dallin H. Oaks presided over the Philippines Area, 2002-04; Quentin L. Cook served in the Area Presidency in the Philippines.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Neil L. Andersen (Brazil South Area, 2001-05) and Ulisses Soares (Brazil Area) lived in Sao Paulo.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Gary E. Stevenson presided over the Japan Nagoya Mission, 2004-07.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: D. Todd Christofferson presided over the Mexico South Area, living in Mexico City.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Dale G. Renlund lived in Johannesburg in the Africa Southeast Area presidency, 2009-14; Ulisses Soares was a counselor there too.

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: Gerrit W. Gong served in the Asia Area presidency, headquartered in Hong Kong, 2011-15.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where between 1 in 40 and 1 in 10 people is a Latter-day Saint (end of 2025 membership).
prompts.text_original: A country where Latter-day Saints were between 1 in 40 and 1 in 10 of the population at the end of 2025 (Church membership figures as of October 2026 divided by UN 2023 population estimates).
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (31 Dec 2025) with UN population estimates (2023, via Wikipedia list)
prompts.summary: Below the one-in-ten group (Tonga, Samoa, American Samoa, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, French Polynesia, the Cook Islands) sits a second tier where members are 1 in 40 to 1 in 10 of the population: Micronesia (1 in 18), Vanuatu (1 in 22), Uruguay, Chile and Cabo Verde (about 1 in 30) and Fiji (1 in 37). New Zealand (1 in 42) and the United States (1 in 49) fall just outside. Ratios use end-of-2025 membership over UN 2023 population estimates.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: 624,203 members, about 1 in 31 of 19.6 million.

answers.name: Fiji
answers.fact: 24,847 members, about 1 in 37 of 919,000.

answers.name: Uruguay
answers.fact: 112,449 members, about 1 in 30 of 3.4 million.

answers.name: Cabo Verde
answers.fact: 16,334 members, about 1 in 32 of 520,000.

answers.name: Vanuatu
answers.fact: 14,042 members, about 1 in 22 of 313,000.

answers.name: Micronesia
answers.fact: 6,241 members, about 1 in 18 of 112,000.
